title: Aivu, a Babylonian in Rav Nachman’s Time
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Bava Metzia 93b, Aivu deposits flax at Bei Dunya. Shabbu—the thief’s name—takes it, and the case comes before Rav Nachman. In Avodah Zarah 35b, Aivu eats gentile bread; Rava, or according to another version Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, says, “Do not mention Aivu,” which Hyman explains as not reporting a teaching in his name. Hyman infers that he was a rabbinic scholar.

notes.text: Hyman glosses the rebuke as not transmitting teachings in Aivu’s name. It is not an instruction merely to stop conversing with him. The scholarly-status conclusion belongs to Hyman.

The consulted Bava Metzia 93b reads Bei Runya, rather than the supplied Bei Dunya. Avodah Zarah 35b says not to converse with Aivu; Hyman interprets the rebuke as not transmitting teachings in his name. The interpretation and the inference about his scholarship remain Hyman’s.
